item.title: Sewage discharge and strong stench raise concerns along Tomanu Road, Nadera
item.description: A strong sewage stench along Tomanu Road in Nadera is raising concerns for residents, with the Nasinu Town Council confirming that sewage from a burst sewer line has been entering a roadside drain. Nasinu Town Council CEO Felix Magnus says the Council inspected the site on the 14th of last month, after receiving a complaint from a resident.
item.content:encoded:
A strong sewage stench along Tomanu Road in Nadera is raising concerns for residents, with the Nasinu Town Council confirming that sewage from a burst sewer line has been entering a roadside drain.

Nasinu Town Council CEO Felix Magnus says the Council inspected the site on the 14th of last month, after receiving a complaint from a resident.

Magnus confirms that the liquid is sewage.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Nasinu resident Ashwani Kumar says the smell is extremely strong and unpleasant, causing significant discomfort and concern in the area.

Kumar says the purplish-brown liquid appears to be entering the drain from somewhere nearby, rather than coming from the drain itself.

He says the source of the discharge should be investigated to determine whether it poses any health or environmental risks to people living and travelling in the area.

When asked whether the Nasinu Town Council is taking any action on the matter, Magnus says the Council was advised that the Water Authority of Fiji had rectified the sewer line on 13th August, but it burst again.

He says the Council referred the matter to WAF, as the sewer line is an asset of WAF.

He says all sewer-related complaints are referred to WAF.

When questioned, WAF says they will visit the site and reconfirm the situation.

item.title: Emotional milestone for siblings as Caginivanua graduates with top award from CATD Nadave
item.description: 19-year-old Apolosa Caginivanua says choosing to walk away from habits that had worried his family and taking a different path has changed his life, as he graduated from CATD Nadave with a qualification in Welding and Fabrication. Caginivanua is one of the two graduates who came through the Inspire Pacific Tagane Mai Programme with support from the Salvation Army, was also named Best Trainee of th
item.content:encoded:
19-year-old Apolosa Caginivanua says choosing to walk away from habits that had worried his family and taking a different path has changed his life, as he graduated from CATD Nadave with a qualification in Welding and Fabrication.

Caginivanua is one of the two graduates who came through the Inspire Pacific Tagane Mai Programme with support from the Salvation Army, was also named Best Trainee of the Year.

The two overcame personal challenges to receive their Level 3 certificates in Welding and Fabrication, as well as FNU NPTC Trade Test Class 3 qualifications.

Caginivanua , who is from Kadavu and shares maternal links to Ra, was emotional as he received his certificate, saying that graduating alongside his fellow students was a proud moment and he is happy to now have a skill that can help him provide for his family.

Before joining CATD Nadave, Caginivanua says he had been involved in some negative habits that had left his family worried about his future.

He says deciding to leave those habits behind and join the school put him on a different path, however, the journey was not easy.

He says his family, particularly his sister, continued encouraging him to complete his training and not turn back.

That made the graduation especially emotional for his sister as she watched her younger brother walk onto the stage to receive his certificate and special award.

She says the achievement means everything to their family after seeing the challenges her younger brother had gone through.

She says there was a time when his choices had left the family worried about where his life was heading, and she never imagined she would one day be sitting beside him as he celebrated such an achievement.

The moment carried even greater significance for the siblings as they have lost both their parents.

His sister says their parents would have been proud to see Caginivanua graduate and receive the Best Trainee award.

She says she was overjoyed when one of his teachers told her that her younger brother would not only graduate but would also receive a special award.

She thanked CATD Nadave, the Salvation Army and everyone who supported Caginivanua throughout his journey.

Now equipped with a qualification in Welding and Fabrication, Caginivanua is encouraging young people facing challenges not to give up on themselves.

He says there will be ups and downs along the way, but young people can change the direction of their lives and achieve their goals if they are willing to put their hearts into it.

item.title: Cabinet backs CWM Hospital redevelopment over $5.35B Valelevu hospital plan

item.content:encoded:
Cabinet has endorsed a staged redevelopment of the existing Colonial War Memorial Hospital after a preliminary plan estimated that building a new National Tertiary Hospital at Valelevu would cost about $5.35 billion.

The Preliminary Master Plan for the proposed Valelevu hospital estimated the project would cost about FJD$5.35 billion, with about FJD$1.4 billion required for the first stage of construction.

Cabinet says given the significant upfront investment required and limited financing commitments, the next stages of planning will instead focus on redeveloping the existing CWM Hospital site.

The staged approach would allow critical hospital infrastructure to be progressively upgraded while health services continue to operate.

It would also allow the Government to spread investment across several budget cycles and pursue financing from development partners.

Cabinet says the redevelopment would support the integration of other planned health investments at the CWM campus, including oncology and radiotherapy infrastructure.

The Feasibility Study and Business Case will now proceed on the basis of a staged redevelopment of CWM Hospital as the Government looks to strengthen Fiji's national tertiary health infr astructure.
